title: Omit the Tumtum
tagline: Take the Gemara's red pen to six baraitot, refill Rabbi Elazar's list of five, test where a tumtum animal urinates, and trace the tumtum through betrothal and ḥalitza
mechanic: Red-pen strike-the-word editor over six baraitot (with one where omission is wrong) + count-then-refill list repair + species/place/sage urination-test toggles with outcome lamp + Eliezer/Akiva switch selecting the yibum baraita (42a:1–42b:18)

title: Three Little Words "From"
tagline: Run animals through the min sieve of Leviticus 1, see why the Torah can't spare a single "from," build the three kinds of garav by moisture, and flip Rava's hermaphrodite switch
mechanic: Conveyor-belt min sieve (which "from" excludes which animal) + fewer-words what-would-you-still-allow reasoning quiz + inside/outside moisture toggle boil builder for three garavs + Rava definite-vs-"if you say" switch with consequence lamps (flogging, priest's claim)

title: Ila's Inspection Day
tagline: Compare the Shushan cubit rods, mash a sac and argue with Rabbi Akiva, flip Rav Pappa's even-if switches, count the joints of a tail, and pick the three blemishes Ila added at Yavne
mechanic: Cubit-rod length comparison + sac-mash-then-slaughter stepper (Akiva vs Yoḥanan ben Nuri) + Rav Pappa's two-feature even-if toggle panels (round hoof, overlapping lip, curly tail) + kid/lamb joint-count slider with Rav Huna's refuted version crossed out + pick-three-of-seven Ila's additions (40a:1–40b:8)

title: Outside or Inside?
tagline: Slide an X-ray across a firstborn’s head to find which blemishes show, flip the feeding switches the Gemara leaves unresolved, drag a missing kidney along the sacrifice timeline, and mark which blemishes three sages count
mechanic: Outside/X-ray layer slider revealing hidden defect markers + teiku switch panel with certain/unresolved lamps + sacrifice-timeline slot picker + sage-by-blemish red/green grid + Beit Shammai/Hillel tassel toggle. Six head cases (nostril hole visible outside vs inside, outer row of the lip per Rav Pappa, external gums, inner gums damaged vs extracted) ruled permit/not, then the three-sage split on extracted inner gums (39a:8–14); six feeding switches (before/after eating and drinking, tied, alone, city, garden per Rav Ashi) that all stand unresolved, Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak’s equal thirds, and Pineḥas’s retroactive-blemish question over redemption money (39a:1–7); Rav Aḥadvoi’s internal-limb dilemma narrowed to disqualification, then dropping the missing kidney before slaughter, before collection, or after collection (Rabbi Yoḥanan, Rav via Rabbi Zeira, Rabbi Yehoshua), Rava’s hours-disqualify, and the rejected stones baraita (39a:15–39b:11); a 3×4 grid for Rabbis Yehuda, Eliezer ben Ya’akov and Yosei on bruised/crushed/torn/cut stones and penis, the pouch per Rabbi Elazar, and a tassel diagram of Beit Shammai’s eight strings and four fingerbreadths vs Beit Hillel’s six and three (39b:12–16)

title: Sunken or Floating?
tagline: Lay Beit Hillel’s sela over Beit Shammai’s drilled hole, paint which parts of a cup an impure liquid defiles, sweep a lens across a firstborn’s eye to tell a sunken cataract from a floating one, and paint the three-month moist-then-dry fodder trial
mechanic: Coin-over-hole size slider with dispute/stringency lights + tap-to-paint vessel impurity zones + draggable magnifier-lens eye exam + half-month fodder calendar painter. Five voices sizing Beit Hillel’s sela against Beit Shammai’s skull hole (Rav Ḥisda’s challenge from the window mishna, the hole-and-its-obstruction answer affirmed by Rav Taḥlifa, Rav Pappa’s large drill per Rabbi Meir and per the Rabbis, Rav Naḥman’s Nero sela) with lights for a real dispute and for Beit Shammai being the stricter per the Eduyot principle, plus the vetch in-and-out derivation (37b:20–38a:2, 16–20); eight vessels (earthenware cup touched outside/inside, flat earthenware, wooden cup with sheretz outside, impure liquid outside per Kelim 25:6 and inside, Ḥizkiyya’s flat sitting bench, flat earthenware slab) where the player paints inside/outside/rim/ear-handle/straight-handle or upper/underside impure, then the zav-fluids decree, the burn-no-teruma sign, why one sign suffices, and the sack/midras requirement (38a:3–15); six eyes searched with an SVG clip-path lens for black/white sunken/floating cataracts per Yoshiya of Usha’s barka mnemonic, the black thread into the white ruled for Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yosei, and the snail-is-the-snake growth, then Lakonya’s sit-my-son and Rav Huna’s ruled-before-the-incident (38a:21–38b:9); pale spots and tears attributed to Rabbi Yehuda, the incomplete mishna on rain-fed vs irrigated fodder, painting Rav Yitzḥak bar Ashiyan’s four months then the Gemara’s Adar-and-half-Nisan / Elul-and-half-Tishrei three, and the unresolved in-season dilemma (38b:10–18)

title: Is It Not I Who Gave It to You?
tagline: Who is believed about a firstborn’s blemish? Find the better lie the renter could have told, predict the showdown at Yavne, catch where Giddul garbled the teaching, and force Rafram’s sore eyes open to recognize his own firstborn
mechanic: Baraita emendation gap + miggo road map + predict-the-answer Yavne showdown with murmur meter + believed/not-believed agent stamps + garbled-transmission tile spotter + hold-to-unblur recognition hunt with eye strain + seat-the-priest verdicts + tithe-gate flock counter + three-laymen condition bench. Rav Ashi’s emendation of the school of Menashe (hearsay valid wherever a woman is) and Mareimar’s jab at Yeimar (36a:2–4); tapping Neresh as the renter’s better lie on an SVG map of the Nehar Pekod and Neresh roads, Abaye’s no-miggo-where-witnesses, the priest’s obvious-blemish miggo and the certainty-vs-concern distinction for Rabbi Ile’a (36a:5–11); predicting Rabbi Yehoshua’s yes, Rabban Gamliel’s no, Rabbi Yehoshua’s public no and his living-can’t-contradict-the-living concession, then a murmur meter until the crowd stops Ḥutzpit (36a:12–16); Demai 4:5 agents (trustworthy-seller vs named seller) and the rejected proof from the mishna (36a:17–36b:3); marking the three tiles Giddul flipped in Rav Yehuda’s version to restore Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba’s Israelite version, the grown-animal novelty, and the ruling like even the first version (36b:4–6); holding to force Rafram’s eyes open against an eye-strain meter and tapping the remembered white star and black foreleg (not the new nicked ear), then only-this-one-is-brazen (36b:7–8); priest-present verdicts for an undetermined blemish vs Rav Ashi’s lopsided eyes (36b:9–12); counting a flock through the gate where the blemished lamb can’t be pushed to tenth (lo yevaker) and the blemish-the-whole-flock reason (36b:13–15); a four-case bench for the first tanna as narrowed by Rava (clear-cut only) and Rav Yehuda (no expert present) vs Rabbi Yosei (36b:16–21)

title: The Quaestor’s Dagger
tagline: Stamp the quaestor’s first cut and the copycats, reword what the bystanders said, time a kick at a charging firstborn, blemish a kid before its head emerges, and decide which shepherds and household members can testify.
mechanic: Copycat stamp sequence + bystander speech-bubble reword grid + real-time kick-timing track + birth-emergence scrubber + flip-reading witness grid with motive pins + household bench lineup. Four incident cards (the quaestor’s first slit ear, his later copycat slits, the children’s torn tail, the copycat tail-tiers) stamped permitted/prohibited, the tzerikhuta for both stories, and the kol she-hu leda’at clauses adding gerama and mesi’aḥ lefi tumo (35a:2–9); toggling the bystanders’ answer between “unless it had a blemish” and “if a blemish was made” while ruling under Rav Ketina and Rava (35a:6–7); an SVG ram charges then stops on a looping pursuit bar and the player kicks once in each phase, ruling each kick under both versions of Rav Pappa (35a:10–13); a slider scrubs a firstborn out of the birth canal and the player blemishes the first visible part before the head emerges for a kid (ear), a lamb per Rava (lip) and per “some say” (ear via the temples), plus Rava’s bleating-mouth blemish as an explanation of the 39a mishna (35a:14–16); a reading toggle flips the mishna’s Israelite-shepherd/priest-shepherd cases between the two amoraic readings while the player stamps three witnesses credible or not and pins the motive (mouthful/legima, “he won’t pass me over”, “he’ll give it to a scholar”, reciprocity), then Rabbi Meir’s novelty via Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kefusai (35a:17–35b:6); a bench table seating market Israelite, market priest, son, daughter and wife under Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kefusai, Rabbi Yosei and the halakha per Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel (wife like himself), Rava’s owners-outside case, and Rav Naḥman’s accepted 18b proof over the rejected tithe proof for doubtful firstborns (35b:5–15)

title: Fined in What He Did
tagline: Flip a lens between how the Torah is written and how it is read, find the Rabbi Shimon Shmuel meant, sentence the ear-slitter and the spot-cutter, add one vav to a bridegroom’s week, and decide whether a fine outlives the father.
mechanic: Ktiv/kri lens toggle + layer sort + redundancy check + 2×2 sentencing bench with void-the-act SVG panels + removable-vav word tile over a seven-day strip + heir wax-seal pass-down. A lens flips תרומתי and בבגדו between spelling and vocalized reading while the player puts four derivations (Rabbi Eliezer’s two terumot, Rabbi Yehoshua’s terumati, Rabbi Akiva’s bigdo, Rabbi Eliezer’s bagad) on the masoret or mikra layer, exposing Rabbi Eliezer on both, resolved by the “lekha / perhaps Elijah will come” reframing (34a:2–6); the dough-for-the-dog kol mum baraita and which Rabbi Shimon Shmuel meant, mishna (redundant with davar she-eino mitkaven) vs. baraita (34a:1, 7–9); a bench where the player sentences the firstborn ear-slitter and the Nega’im 7:5 baheret-cutter under Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis, the crossing heavy sentences flagged, Rabba and Rav Yosef’s property-vs-body deterrent, and Rava’s “fined in what he did” worked by voiding each act on an SVG lamb (slit stops counting, second blemish permits) and skin (excised spot returns, whole-body spread purifies) (34a:10–34b:7); a vav slot toggling yit’har/veyit’har while the player predicts the bridegroom’s seven wedding days pure or impure, ending in a teiku stamp (34b:8–12); five father-dies cases (slave sold to gentiles, planned Chol HaMoed labor, Sabbatical-fertilized field, defiled taharot per Abaye, the slit firstborn) where a wax seal drops to the son or dies with the father, plus the reason (34b:13–35a:1)

title: The Free Wire
tagline: Price tithe meat into the bones of an ox, patch a switchboard of verbal analogies between tithe, firstborn and ḥaramim until one “it shall not be redeemed” runs free, throw Rav Ashi’s alive/slaughtered lever, and seat the guests at a blemished firstborn’s table.
mechanic: Switchboard patch-panel puzzle + alive/slaughtered lever toggle grid + seat-the-guests table. Five-item price-tag sort (sell as meat / fold into price / no sale) for adult vs. orphans’ tithe meat and small vs. large animal bones, with Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzḥak’s “according to the blessing” verse (32a:1–6); an SVG three-jack switchboard (tithe לא יגאל, ḥaramim, firstborn לא תפדה) where the player cuts each proposed gezeira shava by plugging in the Gemara’s refutation card (חלים על הכל, קדוש לפניו ולאחריו, קדושתו מרחם, plus decoys), discovers the superfluous והעברת wire holds and frees the tithe’s phrase, then blocks the firstborn via פדיה≠גאולה, Rabbi Yishmael’s veshav/uva objection, the limiting ״הוא״, and Rava’s owner/kohen ḥaramim shortcut (32a:7–32b:1); a lever that flips the tithe animal alive↔slaughtered while the player sets temura and the Torah sale ban for each state per Rav Ashi, then the standing-and-valuation vs. kal va-ḥomer question and why not write לא ימכר (32b:2–8); two tables (Beit Shammai, Beit Hillel per Rabbi Akiva) where kohen/Israelite/gentile are seated, plus the breast-and-thigh source (32b:9–11).

title: Say It in My Name
tagline: Open the door for the returning ḥaver, judge your own flock without a stake, choose market or home for blemished offerings, fold tithe meat into the price of its horns, and build the citation chains that make a scholar’s lips move in the grave.
mechanic: Opinion-row door grid + stake-gauge escape valves + two-switch stall stamping with a balance-beam pan + Abaye/Rava reader-toggle price tags + citation-chain builder with animated lips and grape pile. Four opinions on the returning ḥaver (R. Meir, R. Yehuda, the ika d’amrei version, R. Shimon & R. Yehoshua ben Korḥa) as rows of open/shut doors, plus Rav Yosef vs. Rabba on the repentant tax collector (31a:1–6); four self-inspection cases where the player rules trust/no-trust then picks the escape hatch (annul the vow, blemish the herd before tithing, eat it while impure) that drains a personal-stake gauge, and the single-expert question (31a:7–12); three blemished animals stamped market+litra vs. home+estimate and an SVG scale for weighing firstborn portion against chulin portion, plus how the Temple benefits via the redemption price (31a:14–31b:5); orphans’/adult tithe and the Sabbatical etrog priced sell/fold-in/no-sale under each reader, then evident vs. not-evident and Rava’s temurah derivation (31b:12–20); six tap-in-order chains of transmission (Rav Sheshet, R. Yitzḥak of Kfar Akko←R. Yoḥanan, Rav Ḥisda←R. Yoḥanan, Rav Yehuda←Rav, R. Yoḥanan←RSBY, R. Yitzḥak bar Ze’eiri) with decoys (31a:3, 9; 31b:9–11).

title: Buy the Truth, Don’t Sell It
tagline: Set Ila’s fee so no one can suspect him, rule on paid judges and paid purification water, pay a carpenter for his idle day, blow your way across a beit haperas, and shop at the suspects’ stalls.
mechanic: Incentive-policy toggles with a suspicion gauge + issar coin counter + consequence-jar verdict deck + compensation tray and wage slider + blow-then-step grid walk + buy/pass market stalls + knife-vs-mouse hide inspection. Tap issar coins to set Ila’s Yavne fees (four for a small animal, six for a large) and pick effort as the reason (29a:1–2), then toggle three payment rules (paid on blemish / paid on unblemished / paid again on re-examination) while an SVG needle swings to the suspicion each policy invites, sealing only the once-either-way ordinance (29a:3–4); eight sequential verdicts on the paid judge and witness (void, Deut. 4:5 for free), paid sprinkling and sanctifying while a jar of mei ḥatat greys to cave water and burnt ash, the Kiddushin 58a contradiction and Abaye’s bringing-and-filling answer, and Prov. 23:23 buy-but-don’t-sell (29a:5–11); the impure kohen’s food/drink/oil tray, the elder on a donkey, a zuz slider for Rashi’s three-zuz carpenter (one zuz) and the pearl-driller’s small discount for Abaye’s idle laborer of that work (29a:6, 29b:3); an 8×4 dust grid where blowing on each square pushes hidden barley-grain bones aside per Rashi before the kohen steps, with a risk mode that can land him on a bone, Rashi’s no-teruma via Chagiga 25b, the trodden beit haperas, and the other-impurities answer (29a:12–29b:2); fourteen buy/pass items across the firstborn, Sabbatical-Year and teruma suspects’ stalls (deer meat, tanned vs untanned hides, female hides per the first tanna vs Rabbi Eliezer, bleached wool, spun yarn, felt, combed flax, chain-work, water and salt per Rabbi Yehuda vs Rabbi Shimon, fish innards) (29b:4–14), closed by spotting the knife-cut hide among the mouse-bitten ones and a cliffhanger on the suspected butcher (29b:15)

title: Your Donkey Is Gone, Tarfon
tagline: Test three readings of the thirty-day clock against one baraita, seal post-mortem blemish rulings, write the bill, find the judge's hand, and get Rabbi Tarfon off the hook at Yavne.
mechanic: Falsification board + post-mortem two-seal verdicts + coin-slider bill + error↔hand matching + gated liability flowchart router + two-key reason lock. Three readings of the first-year blemish (twelve months only; Rabbi Elazar’s second version, year + thirty days from Deut. 15:20 ‘year by year’; his first version, thirty days from the blemish) each have the player predict the deadline for a blemish fifteen days before year-end, plotting colored markers against the baraita’s +15 pin on an SVG timeline and striking the refuted readings (mesayya vs teyuvta, 28a:5–11), then a blemish-day slider shows the resulting deadline; an SVG lamb whose cornea clouds after death beside four cards where the player sets Rabbi Meir’s and Rabbi Yehuda’s seals (body blemish after slaughter, cornea blemish, cornea with witnesses per Rabbi Yoshiya of Usha’s ‘some change’, the non-expert’s buried firstborn) (28a:12–28b:5); coin sliders paying a quarter for a lamb and a half for a bull with Rav Pappa’s and Rav Aḥa bar Ika’s small-livestock-decree reasons (28b:6–7); matching the mishna’s four judicial errors to the Gemara’s with-his-hand acts (Rav, Ravina’s collateral, the sheretz, mixing produce), then routing four docket cases through mishna-error / court-expert / own-hand gates to revoked, exempt, pays, or garmi-only-for-Rabbi-Meir (28b:8–11); closed by the womb-removed cow, Todos’s Alexandrian proof, and a lock that opens only on Rabbi Akiva’s ḥada ve-od reasons (error in an explicit mishna is reversed; an expert for the court is exempt) (28b:12–16)

title: Rav Huna's Cellar
tagline: Sort six real teruma rulings from outside the Land, run Rav Huna's perpetual wine-nullification vat, then decode the firstborn's own-year rule from shana b'shana.
mechanic: Ruling dispatch + animated fraction vat + year-calculation quiz. Six verdict cards for tovas hana'ah (Israelite-to-Israelite vs. kohen paying for teruma rights) and Shmuel's three leniencies (majority nullification, eat-then-separate, only bodily-impure forbidden, touching always permitted) from Bekhorot 27a:2–9; a five-step animated bar-vat walkthrough of Rav Huna bar Rav Yehoshua's perpetual nullification technique (pour 2 chulin + 1 teruma, nullify, take out 1, add new teruma, repeat) with a CSS sweep animation on nullification (27a:7); and three year-calculation questions on the firstborn's birth-year rule (shana b'shana = the animal's own year not the calendar, two days and one night for the unblemished firstborn like a peace offering, and Lev. 12:6's 'its year' derivation) from Bekhorot 27b:3–7.

title: Give It to Me
tagline: Run a firstborn nursery while the kohen knocks too early, rebuild Rava's three wool disputes, find the one tanna who fits the dangling-wool mishna, and press a fleece to see which strands stick out.
mechanic: Day-ticker nursery calendar + three-cell dispute board + suspect lineup + fleece press. Seven knocks at the pen gate: a day marker runs along a strip flagged at 30 days, 50 days and Rabbi Yosei's three months, and the player hands over or keeps tending the firstborn lamb/kid/calf when the kohen says 'give it to me' (too early, after the window, the same day-45 lamb under the first tanna vs Rabbi Yosei, a blemished kid 'so I may eat it', an unblemished lamb 'and I will sacrifice it' in Temple times), with Rav Sheshet's threshing-floor-helper reason (26b:8, 16–17) and Rav Kahana's/Rava's readings of Exod. 22:28–29 for 30/50; a year-clock round on blemishes inside vs after the first twelve months (26b:9); Rava's 3×2 board where the player cycles Disputed / All permit / All forbid for the first tanna, Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yosei over slaughtered vs died blemished firstborns whose shed wool was set in a compartment (26a:2–8); Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak's proof as six Fits / Doesn't-fit suspects (Yosei/Yehuda × slaughtered/died × Akavya/Rabbis) until only the Rabbis-in-slaughter survive (26a:9–13); an SVG fleece with twelve strands where a press plate flattens the compressible ones, ruled per Reish Lakish (root turned outward) and Rav Natan bar Oshaya (doesn't press down), plus Rabbi Ile'a's no-fleece-without-loose-hairs reason (26b:5–6); Rabbi Yannai's shelf sorting sin/guilt/firstborn/tithe/burnt offerings' self-shed wool and the rejected 'plucks' proof (26a:14–26b:4); closed by the threshing-floor helpers baraita (desecrated, Num. 18:32's death penalty, why the Sages didn't fine them) (26b:18–20)

title: The Last Eater
tagline: Slide a rotting carcass down a line of eaters to see when it stops being food, rule whether swallowed impurity can wake, find the brine suspicion threshold, then sort which mishna Rav meant.
mechanic: Feeding-line threshold: a rot slider and a line of eaters (dog, ger toshav) decide when a carcass stops counting as impure, ruled per sage and severity. Plus a sorting game for Abaye objections and a candidate sorter for which mishna Rav rule is about.

title: When Kind Finds Kind
tagline: Watch a fetus vanish into a clot, wait for couriers to explain three skeins of yarn, test a sealed jar of fish brine in two possible worlds, then pour it into a pot and watch swallowed impurity wake up.
mechanic: Canvas particle-jar lab + sage lamp board + courier-relay label rack + two-worlds sealed-jar simulation + predict-then-run pot revival + mix-and-lift grain pile with a preparation sorter. A clot jar of a few pale flesh particles among many blood particles (Rashi) where the player rules exempt-from-firstborn yes / impurity by contact or carrying no, and the flesh recolors into the majority for Rabbi Yoḥanan's bittul be-rov (22a:1–2), then picks the burial reason (to publicize) and Rabbi Shimon's matching afterbirth ruling with its first-tanna contrast (22a:3–4); three cases where the player lights lamps for Rabbi Meir (warp skein), Rabbi Yehuda (woof skein) and Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Tzadok (tefifiyot) on when a stillborn opens the grave, plus the Jerusalem mule image (22a:5–6); couriers ride an SVG road from the Land of Israel (Rav Huna's two skeins, Rav Dimi's three, Ravin's explanation, the Gemara's clod) unlocking labels the player taps onto warp / woof / sack-makers' skeins, and the Bethlehem jug stopper (22a:7–8); two side-by-side canvases of fish brine (water-majority vs brine-majority) touched to the mikveh with a hashaka wave, ruled per Reish Lakish's mi-mah nafshakh with Rashi on why hashaka purifies water but not brine (22a:9–10); the brine-majority world used for dipping bread vs poured into a pot, predicted then animated as the swallowed water finds its kind and its impurity rings return (Rabbi Yirmeya, 22a:11), and Rav Dimi's Terumot 5:2 proof picked over Abaye's red-heifer ashes; closed by mixing one impure se'a into a hundred, lifting one out for Rabbi Eliezer's 'the se'a that fell is the se'a that rose', sorting seven preparations (dry, roasted, fruit juice, small doughs vs one big water dough, rinsing, wine) under the Rabbis, and a page-turn to 23a's Ulla decree and Abaye's 'does purity wake impurity?' (22b:1–3)

title: Under the Rod
tagline: Open the four gates Rabbi Shimon’s kid might take into the tithe pen, play the Gemara’s mnemonic tiles in a tug-of-war between firstborn and sacrifices, send for a wise shepherd, and decode what a silent seller’s silence means to Rav, Shmuel and Rabbi Yoḥanan.
mechanic: Aramaic-clue gate board + mnemonic-tile tug-of-war with decoys and a verse bridge + expert lineup + silent-seller thought-bubble decoder + cliffhanger page-turn. Four gate cards (Ze’eiri’s thirty days, incomplete months, part of a day, a kid under eight days entering the pen) are opened one per round by matching the Gemara’s own Hebrew/Aramaic line for each ve-i ba’it eima reading of Rabbi Shimon vs. the first tanna (21a:2–5); each new reading welds the previous gate shut for both sides, except the fourth, which flips the part-of-a-day gate open for both; a follow-up ties gate four to Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda’s baraita (21b:1). Then ten shuffled tiles (גואל, מום, תמורה, אכילה toward the firstborn; זכר, קדוש, במתנות, פשוט toward sacrifices, per Rashi; plus a circular-reasoning decoy and a false ‘both eaten by kohanim’ decoy) are played left, right or out while an SVG rope knot marked מעשר slides, ending dead even at 4–4 before the player picks the העברה/העברה gezera shava (Ex. 13:12 ↔ Lev. 27:32) over Lev. 22:27 and the redemption verses (21b:2–3); a four-step shepherd round on Rava’s detzalta vs. Shmuel’s blood bubbles, Rav Pappa’s wise shepherd, and Rav Ḥisda’s unresolved forty-day question with Ze’eiri’s receptivity deflection (21b:4–5); three Amora cards where the player fills the Jewish seller’s thought bubble (boast / thinks it’s for slaughter / would warn of a prohibition) and rules definite firstborn / doubtful / definitely ḥullin for Rav, Shmuel and Rabbi Yoḥanan, then the oto-ve’et-beno baraita resolved as seller-duty vs. buyer-duty (21b:6–8); closed by Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov’s buried clot, Rabbi Ḥiyya’s no-impurity teaching, and a page-turn to 22a:1’s ‘to publicize’ answer and Rabbi Yoḥanan’s nullification

title: The Goat’s First Year
tagline: Find the hidden hinge under five readings of Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Yehoshua, watch a goat’s year turn on a ring calendar around Ze’eiri’s thirty days, swap the nameplates on the milk dispute, and breed ten kids into the tithe pen
mechanic: progressive hinge-lock + ring-calendar dial + nameplate swap + majority-slice bar + litter-tree breeding counter. Five rounds over the goat bought from a gentile where both sides are fixed (kohen vs. owner) and the player picks the real hinge from six, with already-agreed hinges locked as the Gemara narrows: unseen tinuf (trap: seen tinuf, the rejected ‘shall we say’), Rava’s Rabbi-Meir objection answered by concern-only-for-stringency (20a:6–8), recovery to give birth in year one (20a:9), Ze’eiri’s thirty days (20a:10–12), incomplete months (20a:13–20b:1), part of a day (20b:2); for the last three an SVG twelve-month ring with Ze’eiri’s red band animates conception→birth arcs for the Rabbis-per-Rabbi-Yehoshua vs. Rabbi Yehoshua himself, including the day-30/day-31 conception landing on the last day of year one vs. day one of year two; then Rabbi Ḥanina of Sura’s milk case with player-set nameplates for Akiva/Yehoshua, a draggable-share miscarry/girls/boys bar where the player taps the slices that free the widow per Rabbi Yehoshua in Yevamot 119a (miscarriages joined to girls make boys a minority), and the ‘reverse it’ answer that physically swaps the nameplates (20b:3–7); closed by a 0–3 litter picker for a mother kid and her daughters filling a pen to ten, the 3-3-2-2 why-all-triplets question, and the mother-bears-again shortcut whose absence proves a goat doesn’t give birth twice in a year (20b:8–9)

title: Two Keys to the Womb
tagline: Drop newborns through three verse-sieves, turn the two keys of a firstborn for Rabbi Tarfon and Rabbi Akiva, fire a counterexample at Ravina, draw Rabbi Yishmael’s age lines for a goat bought from a gentile, and sort the majorities you can see from the ones you can’t
mechanic: three-verse sieve drop + two-key verdict board + counterexample cannon + age-line year tracks + evident/non-evident majority street sort. Five newborns fall one at a time and the player picks which phrase of the baraita’s kelal-u-perat catches each (‘firstborn’, ‘male’, ‘opens the womb’, or through to the kohen), including Abaye’s reading that ‘opens the womb’ excludes the caesarean animal itself (19a:4–7); a two-key display (first out / opens the womb) for the caesarean male and the male after it, ruled under Rabbi Tarfon (both graze, eaten blemished by the owner) and Rabbi Akiva (neither is a firstborn) (19a:2–3); Rav Sherevya’s contradiction, Abaye vs Ravina attributions, then firing one of three birth orders at Ravina’s superfluous-word theory until Rav Aḥa of Difti’s caesarean-female case cracks it (19a:6–19b:3); per-species 1–5 year tracks where the player taps the last certain year for goat/ewe/cow/donkey per Rabbi Yishmael (with Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda’s fourth-year donkey from 20a), then Rabbi Akiva’s tinuf/shilya signs and his known/unknown/doubt rule (19b:5–7); closed by an SVG street of nine kosher shops and one non-kosher shop and a sort of five majorities into in-front-of-us vs statistical, the minors-and-yibum challenge, Rabbi Meir’s concession on ḥalitza, and the 20a cliffhanger resolution with Rava and Ravina’s act-dependent majority

title: The Lambing Pen of Perhaps
tagline: Slide a corpse to the exact midpoint between two towns, build every possible world in an unwatched lambing pen to find what the kohen is guaranteed, split the plump lamb from the lean one, and load the gift tray for Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yosei
mechanic: precision-tape slider + premise-grid deduction + possible-worlds enumeration pen + jurisdiction-courtyard parable toggle + gift-tray loader. A range slider moves a slain body between two towns while a wobbling tape refuses to read an exact tie (the Rabbis: impossible to be precise); a 2×2 grid of premises (precision possible/impossible × kerova excludes/includes several towns) where the player derives no heifer / two heifers / one shared heifer with a stipulation, then seats the first tanna, Rabbi Eliezer and Rav Amram’s Rabbis in their cells (18a:2–6); seven unwatched lambing nights from the new mishna (two first-timers bearing 2M, M+F, 2M+F, 2F+M, 2M+2F; one experienced + one first-timer bearing 2M, M+F) where the player taps newborns into each ewe’s birth order to build worlds, tracks the lowest kohen yield found, declares the guaranteed count, and an exhaustive enumerator reveals the worst world (‘perhaps both bore females first’); a plump/lean hand-out under Rabbi Tarfon (better one to the kohen) and Rabbi Akiva per Rabbi Yoḥanan (kohen takes the lean; meshammenin = the shumman is disputed), the one-died contradiction resolved by Rabbi Ami’s retraction, Rabbi Ḥiyya’s shepherd and homeowner folds, and an SVG courtyard whose corner shades to the kohen when Rabbi Tarfon grants him a share (Rava/Rav Pappa, 18b:10–12); closed by toggling the foreleg/jaw/maw tray for Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yosei across the replacement-with-kohen case, Rabbi Elazar’s kohen-got-nothing case, and Rav Pappa’s uncertain-tithe case, each with its ‘lest you say’ pick

title: Whose Lamb Is It?
tagline: Count out Rabbi Tarfon's sela, shekel and ragya, pass lambs, donkeys and grain piles from hand to hand until someone is left holding them, then unlock why Rav Naḥman needed both of his inheritance rulings
mechanic: coin-purse composer + pass-the-parcel custody relay + two-dial tzerichuta lock. Tap sela/shekel/dinar/ma'a coins into a purse to pay exact amounts: Rabbi Tarfon's generous sela, miserly shekel and middle ragya (Rava: three dinars, ragil here and there), the one-ma'a lean lamb that works for one who acts on his own (vs. the ragya for one who comes to ask), and the donkey's full value when there's no lamb (Reish Lakish via Ravina's not-stricter-than-hekdesh, with Rav Naḥman son of Rav Yosef's boiled-vegetables option); then ten custody chains where a token steps hand to hand across an animated track before the player rules who ends up holding it: a stranger redeeming another's donkey (owner, by the thief's double-payment proof), ten doubtful donkeys' lambs (tithed and kept), the kohen's gift lamb (exempt from tithe), donkeys and tevel inherited through a kohen maternal grandfather (kept), gentile-smoothed vs. Jew-smoothed piles bought from a gentile (exempt by 'your grain' vs. tithed-and-his), produce deposited with a Samaritan vs. a gentile (Demai 3:4 and Rabbi Elazar's framing), and the lamb that died before reaching the kohen (his from separation); closed by a lock that opens only when both dials name the real tzerichuta reasons (lambs stand separated vs. grain tithed from itself)

title: The Donkey Nobody Redeemed
tagline: Sort carcasses between village and market and watch 'its prohibition is its intent' collapse, scrub a firstborn donkey from birth to the cleaver under Rabbi Yehuda and two readings of Rabbi Shimon, then balance the scale that decides whether a woman is betrothed with it
mechanic: village/market placement map + contradiction-finder + life-cycle timeline scrubber + legal-tool rack + balance-scale physics toy. Eight Okatzin 3:3 carcasses (non-kosher horse anywhere, kosher nevela anywhere, kosher bird and chelev in villages vs. markets, Rabbi Shimon's pig) drop onto a two-zone map and are ruled already-food vs. needs-intent, then the player multi-selects every ruling that refutes the issuro-chishuvo theory before the Gemara's reisha/seifa argument and Rava's conclusion, with a two-reading toggle on Nimos vs. Rabbi Eliezer's practice crow; a range-slider timeline of the firstborn donkey (alive: sale/rent value, alive: shearing/work, redeemed with a lamb, neck broken) where each stop is ruled permitted/forbidden under three lenses (Rabbi Yehuda; Rabbi Shimon per Rabba/Rav Nachman/Reish Lakish; Rabbi Shimon per Rabbi Yochanan), with the neck-break stop gated behind choosing the cleaver-from-behind over the reed/sickle/ax/saw/locked room; Rav Nachman's two proofs (the arifa gezera shava, Levi's lost-money baraita) each judged only-Rabbi-Shimon vs. Rabbi-Yehuda-could-be-the-tanna before Safra's and the Gemara's deflections; and an SVG balance scale for the Kiddushin 56b mishna where the player sets the donkey's value and toggles Rabbi Shimon / Rabbi Yehuda with an any-amount lamb / Rabbi Yehuda with Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda's shekel minimum until nothing is left in her hand (Rav's donkey-worth-a-shekel case), closed by picking Leviticus 27:25 as Rava's source for the shekel over Numbers 18:16's rejected hekesh

title: The Et Hunter
tagline: Shimon HaAmasoni expounded every little 'et' in the Torah until he reached 'Et the Lord your God you shall fear.' Hunt the particles yourself, stack the Gemara's proofs that milk is kosher and watch three of them crack, then climb a ladder of strange-calf dilemmas the Gemara leaves half-open
mechanic: particle-hunt word game + proof-tower judge + narrowest-reading ladder puzzle. Tap every אֶת (and the extra heh of ha-teme'im) across Exodus 20:12, Leviticus 11:4 and 11:31, earning coins for expounding (glosses: Ketubot 103a's stepparents and older brother, Rabbi Shimon's et ha-gamal = camel's milk, the heh = juice, gravy and sediment). Deuteronomy 6:13 unlocks last and forces the withdrawal choice, which sets the withdrawal counter equal to the expounding counter ('just as I received reward for expounding…') before Rabbi Akiva's Torah-scholars reveal. Then sort four camel derivations between Rabbi Shimon and the Rabbis. Next, judge six proofs that milk is kosher as hold or crack, naming the Gemara's objection for each one that cracks (benefit-vs-eating twice, sell-to-buy-food); the three that hold (David's ten cheeses with its 'commerce in wartime?' rebuttal, milk and honey, Isaiah 55:1) stack as bricks on a tower. Finally, pick exactly the rungs that two baraitot must cover in the cow→donkey / donkey→horse / cow→horse chain of dilemmas, where the Gemara narrows both to the first rung, then compare horns and hooves to reach the 'just a red donkey' answer, with an epilogue on Rabbi Shimon's head-and-most-of-the-body rule

title: Double or Nothing
tagline: A Roman officer named Kontrokos accuses Moses of cooking the books — a Levite headcount short 300 men, a treasury missing half its silver. Audit the census yourself, catch the Sanctuary's secret double-weight maneh, sort a litter of mismatched newborns, and unravel a rabbi's wordplay on Rephidim and Shittim
mechanic: forensic-audit ledger puzzle + drag-free verdict sorter + name/derash toggle cards — two real Kontrokos-vs-Rabban-Yoḥanan-ben-Zakkai ledger discrepancies (22,300 individually-counted Levites vs. the Torah's stated 22,000; 201 talents 11 maneh collected vs. 100 talents spent on sockets) worked as multiple-choice audits with full reveals of Abaye's dayo principle and the doubled Sanctuary maneh, plus a live one-sixth-from-the-outside padding slider deriving Ezekiel 45:12's 60-shekel maneh; a six-case litter sorter for the new mishna (cow→donkey-shaped calf, donkey→horse-shaped foal, ewe→goat-shaped lamb with and without partial simanim, ordinary goat kid, camel→kosher-looking newborn) where firstborn status and eating status are guessed as two independently-scored verdicts per case before the daf's real reasoning reveals; and a four-card dialogue between Rabbi Chanina and Rabbi Eliezer toggling between Rabbi Eliezer's literal place-names (Rephidim, Shittim) and Rabbi Yehoshua's derash readings from the parallel baraita

title: Called the People?
tagline: A Levite snatches gifts meant for the kohen and Rav can't decide whether to make him pay: is a Levite counted among "the people" who owe the foreleg, jaw, and maw? Work the gift docket on nine real cases, then follow four failed proofs — one a genuine refutation — before Mareimar closes the file for good, and catch the daf ending mid-sentence on Ulla and the kohenet
mechanic: three-bin repossession docket + multiple-choice doubt-proof gauntlet — nine real cases (untithed teruma, an undelivered foreleg/jaw/maw, gifts already in one kohen's hand, a poor owner keeping his own peret and olelot, withheld maaser ani, a cow's maw sold whole vs. by weight, unclaimed first-shorn wool, and an unsifted stew) sorted into מוֹצִיאִין / אֵין מוֹצִיאִין / פָּטוּר per the daf's actual sanctity, azivah-vs-netina, and intact-object tests, paired with a four-round gauntlet reconstructing Rav's real unresolved doubt over whether Levites are called 'the people' (the nine-kohen-properties baraita, the sanctity-principle baraita, the slaughter-for-whom baraita escalating into an explicit תיובתא, and Rav's own tannaitic-dispute rescue), closing on Mareimar's dual ruling and a click-to-reveal cliffhanger on Ulla, the kohenet, and the mincha law that the daf itself leaves mid-sentence

title: A Hair's Breadth
tagline: A dog that ate from a corpse lies dead across the threshold and four Tannaim rule on the house. Slide it, widen its neck, flip it around until the judges say what each challenge asks (or admit it cannot be done), fill Rabbi Shimon's two-of-three grid, scratch a thigh bone and a creeping thing's egg open by a hair's breadth, and go out and see the orifices, sinews, and seams that decide whether a touch reaches the flesh
mechanic: constraint-satisfaction sandbox with live judges + scratch-off canvas + lens-reveal hidden-object — an SVG doorway scene where the player sets three real variables of Oholot 11:7 as the Gemara reads it (mouth in/out, neck under a handbreadth / a handbreadth counting walls / a handbreadth of hollow, past the doorstop line or on the outer threshold) while four judge tiles rule live (Rabbi Meir on the neck, Rava's Rabbi Yosei on hollow-plus-position, Rabbi Elazar on the exit route, Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira always impure), and seven target-verdict challenges must be satisfied or declared impossible (Yosei-strict-and-Meir-lenient and ben-Beteira-pure are the traps); a 3×3 exactly-two-per-row-and-column logic grid for Rabbi Shimon's mould / barley-bone / golel-and-dofek across contact, carrying, and tent; a destination-out scratch canvas where a hair-thin stroke flips a sealed thigh bone or embryo egg from tahor to tamei, with Rav Oshaya's intent button and an embryo-tissue toggle; and nine cases (hide, kidney in fat, sealed and perforated bone, unbroken and tissueless eggs, half-earth mouse touched on either half, sea mouse) inspected with a draggable clip-path lens that reveals the orifices, sinews, and seams before ruling

title: Between Two Gates
tagline: A validly slaughtered animal is still twitching — out of the category of the living, not yet entered the category of the dead. Rule its ten real laws at the threshold (food impurity but not carcass impurity, the limb versus the flesh that parts from it, Abaye's double stringency, the trap of the invalid slaughter), probe the bird and the beast for the parts that are merely wood, and judge which gathering of alal carries carcass impurity
mechanic: liminal threshold tug-of-war + anatomy pin-probe — a heartbeat nefesh-orb hangs in a doorway between an ember Living Gate and a bone Dead Gate while the player rules the ten real mefarkeset laws of Rav Oshaya's Tosefta and Abaye (takes food impurity, no carcass impurity, separated limb like ever min hachai, separated flesh pure, forbidden to bnei Noach even after death, doesn't shield swallowed items under a corpse's roof, bestiality still liable, Rabbi Yoḥanan over Ḥizkiyya, plus one-siman and stabbing trap cards that collapse the doorway), each correct verdict tugging the orb toward a gate before it drifts back to dead center for Rabbi Zeira's 'left the living, never entered the dead'; opened by numbered pins over bird-and-beast line art ruling beak tip / Rav Pappa's inner membrane, talon tip / base sunk in flesh, and horn shaft / blood-line base as 'joins' or 'merely wood', and closed by picking which of three alal collectors (adult, child, wind) creates carcass impurity per Rav Huna's da'at rule and whether the hide nullifies two clinging half-olives

title: The Soul That Drinks
tagline: Work the alchemist's bench: congeal the blood, melt the forbidden fat, dissolve the chametz, liquefy a bird carcass over fire and over sun — stamp each verdict, then find the stringency that blocks each of the Gemara's attempted derivations, forge the one source-pair that carries consecrated produce, and swing the two exegetical lenses of Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua
mechanic: state-change alchemy bench + refutation forge — eight substances visibly change state in an animated flask (melt over fire, dissolve in water, congeal, rot in the sun) before the player stamps the daf's real verdict (Reish Lakish's three nefesh-includes-the-drinker readings, the sun-rotted carcass that stays pure, the lentil-bulk of sheretz gravy, liquids-don't-join-solids), then a derivation-blocking logic game where the player identifies the shared stringency that refutes each proposed source (karet, no period of fitness, never permitted, any-amount impurity, dayo) and forges the one valid source-pair for hekdesh liquids from bikkurim/teruma/chametz/carcass, capped by an Eliezer/Yehoshua don-minah lens toggle flipping the verdicts on date honey, apple wine, bikkurim beverages, and orla juice

title: The Master Said to Me
tagline: Host one Babylonian evening meal and survive it: patrol the fields at dusk, wash three kinds of waters correctly, wait out the cheese after meat, wipe with the one bread Rabbi Zeira allows, guard your crumbs from the angel of poverty, sink the foam, untie the gardener's bundle, and keep the wine barrel out from under the gutter demon
mechanic: hazard-navigation dinner simulator — an eleven-scene choose-your-action evening meal scored on three meters (guf/body, mamon/purse, ruach/spirit) where every choice is resolved by the daf's actual rulings (Rav Chisda's meat-then-cheese ban, Rabbi Zeira's wiping-bread tests, the first/middle/final waters baraita, Sodomite salt, the held-cup limits), with a signature flip-card after each of Abaye's eight traditions that turns his assumed mundane reason over to reveal Rabba's hidden one (evil spirit, poverty angel, witchcraft, demons), graded on Mar Ukva's vinegar-son-of-wine scale

title: The Angel Who Never Sang
tagline: Stage the angel's grip to see which thigh Yaakov lost, match five Sages to the five verses that keep a scholar indoors after dark, measure the ladder at eight thousand parasangs, and re-cut the angels' Kedushah until the Divine Name lands where the baraita allows it
mechanic: top-down staging puzzle placing the angel in the three real positions the Sages reconstruct (face-to-face hug per Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi and Rashi, at Yaakov's right hand per Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani's gentile and Rava bar Ulla's Torah scholar, or up from behind per the Rabbis) and reading off which thigh each blocking strikes, a five-verse/five-Sage single-use assignment of the sources for a Torah scholar not going out alone at night (Rabbi Yitzchak, Rabbi Abba bar Kahana, Rabbi Abbahu, the Rabbis, Rav), an evidence-dial derivation of the ladder's 8,000-parasang width from the plural of olim/yordim and Tarshish's 2,000, and a Kedushah composer where the player adds and removes kadoshes across three angelic companies until Rav Chananel's 1/1/1 becomes the Gemara's emended 1/2/3, validated live against the baraita's rule that angels may not utter the Name before three words, plus a seven-stop dial through the disputed frequency of the angels' song

title: Larger Than Life
tagline: Catch the Mishnah itself exaggerating across the ash-mound, golden vine, and Curtain, route seven real sciatic-nerve cases through the altar's back rooms, and follow the Gemara's own back-and-forth over whether Rabbi Yehuda was certain or just guessing
mechanic: spot-the-exaggeration reveal across three real Mishnayot (ash-mound, golden vine, Curtain) per Rabbi Yitzchak bar Nachmani/Shmuel's three guzma cases, a routing puzzle sending the sciatic nerve of burnt/peace offerings to their correct real destination (altar ash-mound vs. courtyard drain) per Rav Huna and the Rabbis, and a locked step-by-step reveal of the Gemara's certain-vs-unsure back-and-forth over Rabbi Yehuda's thigh ruling

title: What Are We?
tagline: Match three tzaddikim who called themselves dust, nothing, and a worm against five kings who crowned themselves gods, watch Rava rank humility itself, quiz the brand-new mishnah of gid hanasheh, and solve the ash-of-a-doomed-city riddle that closes the chapter
mechanic: 16-card memory-match grid pairing three self-effacing tzaddikim (Avraham, Moshe & Aharon, David) and five self-aggrandizing kings (Nimrod, Pharaoh, Sancheriv, Nevuchadnetzar, Chiram) to their real verses, followed by an interactive reveal of Rava's ranking that Moshe & Aharon's "what are we" outranks Avraham's "dust and ashes" plus flip-cards on Rabbi Il'a, Rabbi Abbahu, and Rabbi Yitzchak's humility teachings, a true/false quickfire on the six real conditions and two disputes of the brand-new gid hanasheh mishnah, and a step-by-step reveal of the idolatrous-city-ash logic (Ze'eiri's dust-of-its-dust distinction, Rava's mitzvot-lo-lehanot-nitnu, and Rav Ashi's shiur-based resolution) that closes the Kisuy HaDam chapter

title: Dust and Ashes
tagline: Sort sixteen real substances into what covers slaughtered blood and what doesn't, get stranded without earth once in the desert and once on a ship, and meet Beit Hillel and Beit Shammai's fight over whether ash even counts as dust
mechanic: substance sorting game (16 real mishna/baraita items dragged into 'covers'/'does not cover' bins, checked against the min-afar category and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's grows-plants rule) + a desert/ship stranded-without-earth scenario picker (grind a gold dinar or burn your garment for ash) + a sage-position quiz on the dam hanitaz machloket + closing flip-cards on the Beit Hillel/Beit Shammai ash-is-afar dispute and Rava's aggada about Avraham's dust and ashes

title: One Covering for All
tagline: A deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor slaughters unsupervised — fill in Rebbi's real verdict grid, test whether a purity shortcut transfers to forbidden meat, then run animals through one covering pit and watch Rabbi Yehuda split it in two
mechanic: predict-and-reveal verdict grid (2×3 table exposing that the Rabbis actually dispute both clauses of the mishna, not just the one the plain text shows) + true/false twist cards flipping who's really lenient vs. stringent + a mi'ut/chazakah rule-transplant test + a group-and-seal sequencing toy (drop chaya/of tokens into a shared covering under the Rabbis' rule, or under Rabbi Yehuda's order-constrained split)

title: The Redacted Rabbis
tagline: Unmask which sage is hiding behind "the Rabbis" in two mirror-image mishnayot, catch each one's one real exception, and help Rabbi Chiyya outwit the moths in his flax
mechanic: redacted-ruling unmasking (reveal evidence chips, then accuse Rabbi Meir or Rabbi Shimon of hiding behind the mishnah's anonymous "the Rabbis" across two mirror-image rulings on unfit slaughter) + true/false loophole cards testing each sage's one real concession + a branching how-do-you-get-the-blood puzzle from Rabbi Chiyya's moth-eaten flax

title: The Stewpot Ledger
tagline: Slide your fortune from a hundred dinars to ten thousand and watch Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya's stewpot fill — then guess the bracket for six purses, diagnose a cup of lukewarm water, and flip five household maxims from Proverbs
mechanic: wealth-bracket resource simulator + predict-the-tier quiz (drag a log-scale dinar slider through Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya's four stewpot brackets, then guess the right pot and frequency for six purses) plus a branching diagnose-your-cup wizard for Rabbi Yochanan's lukewarm-water rule and a flip-card gallery of five Proverbs-derived household maxims

title: The Litter Ledger
tagline: A firstling drops its afterbirth, a consecrated ewe drops hers — split a hundred births into buckets and watch the majority decide their fate
mechanic: population majority scale (drag a genuine miut anywhere in range and watch Rav Ika's rov/miut bucket-arithmetic hold; toggle firstling vs. consecrated litters to flip which bucket wins)

title: The Convergence Gauge
tagline: Feel out which cords count as the convergence of sinews, then flip switches on three strands and watch Ameimar and Mar bar Rav Ashi disagree in real time
mechanic: diagnostic classifier + live dual-rule strand calculator (sort specimens by Abaye's four tests, then toggle three strands and watch two amoraic AND/OR formulas diverge)

title: The Warning Cry
tagline: Eight slaughters, one day — cry the hatra'ah only at the moment, and about the charge, that makes the lashes stick
mechanic: forewarning timeline (cry or hold your peace at each moment of a day's slaughters; hatra'at safek strikes doubtful cries)

title: The Koy Pen
tagline: Two hybrid kids, two different mothers — sort six real rulings into the right pen, then meet five sages who can't agree what a koy even is
mechanic: sort/spot-the-difference (assign six of Rav Pappa's real rulings to the correct sire×dam pen) + sage-to-claim matching + step-through objection volley

title: The Rispak Stables
tagline: Rabbi Abba wants mules for his wagon — listen to each bray, measure ears and tails, and harness only the ones that match
mechanic: siman inspection (hear synthesized brays, read ears & tails, yoke matching mules; koy-gate epilogue)

title: The Sealed Dockets
tagline: Seven verdict records survived the archive; set the four dials and reconstruct the cases of Oto v'et Beno
mechanic: inverse deduction (read the verdict stamps, set dials to reconstruct the case)

title: The Herdbook Lens
tagline: One womb-born kid becomes a three-generation herd — swing the lens of four poskim over the flock, stamp every page, and outrun the bear
mechanic: posek lens (swing rulings-lenses over one womb-born herd and stamp who needs the knife)

title: The Five-Year Lamb
tagline: Shepherd the ben pekuah from the womb to five years plowing the field — at every waypoint, is it one animal or part of another?
mechanic: waypoint trail (escort one creature through nine stations of its halakhic biography)

title: The Phantom Knife
tagline: Six scenes, one blade that never touches anything: click where the halakhic cut falls
mechanic: phantom-knife scene cuts (place the halakhic cut on an SVG scene, or keep it sheathed)

title: The Severed Link
tagline: Forge four chains of the daf's reasoning, link by link, in the smithy of Pumbedita
mechanic: chain-forging (pick the next link to rebuild the sugya's reasoning)

title: The Swallowed Ring
tagline: You are the posek: rule tamei or tahor on ten real cases of encapsulated impurity
mechanic: verdict cards (judgment quiz)
